newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan wheat buying seen strong - USDA says.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan wheat buying seen strong - USDA says.

text.p: Pakistan wheat demand should remain firm in the 1997/98 season and lower wheat prices may tempt Islamabad to rebuild stocks, an economist with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) said on Thursday.
Traders and industry analysts have estimated that Pakistan's wheat imports could reach as high as four million tonnes.

"I believe the official USDA estimate is still a little less than that simply because there appears to be a very good crop in Pakistan and the demand, while its growing, doesn't appear to require that kind of volume of imports," he told Reuters in an interview.
The U.S. agriculture attache in Pakistan had previously estimated that Pakistan may import three million tonnes of wheat in 1997/98.
Lower wheat prices, though, may tempt Pakistan to step into the market, said the USDA official, who asked not to be named.
"With prices sharply lower, this could be a good period of time for the Pakistani government to rebuild some of their own stocks," he said.
Consumption of wheat products is also growing in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, the USDA said.

Sri Lanka imported around 913,000 tonnes of wheat in 1996 from just over one million in 1995, the Central Bank in Colombo said. Bangladesh wheat imports are estimated to reach one million tonnes this year from 500,000 tonnes last year.
